results.name: Tropic names co-founder Justin Etkin CEO as AI procurement business expands
results.content:
Tropic has named co-founder Justin Etkin as CEO, formalizing a leadership transition at the New York-based procurement technology company as it expands its AI-powered spend intelligence platform for enterprise software buyers. The change, announced August 13, 2026, comes as the company reports a 79% year-over-year increase in bookings and manages more than $23 billion in customer spending.  
Co-founder David Campbell, who led Tropic since its founding, will remain chairman of the board and an active advisor, focusing on go-to-market strategy and corporate initiatives. Etkin, previously Chief Operating Officer, takes responsibility for the company's next stage of growth.  
The succession follows Tropic's shift from a services-led procurement business toward a software and intelligence platform designed to help finance and procurement teams manage increasingly complex software and AI portfolios.
## Founders split responsibilities  
Campbell helped oversee the transition while building the executive team that will support the company's next phase. Tropic said he added senior leadership across finance and marketing while also developing and promoting executives internally.  
"From a spreadsheet prototype to an intelligence platform used by some of the world's most notable companies, we transformed the way technology is purchased," Campbell said. He described Etkin as the right leader for Tropic's next stage.  
For professionals in [AI for Executives & Strategy](https://completeaitraining.com/tag/executives-and-strategy/) roles, the shift signals how procurement data is becoming strategic collateral. Tropic has built a moat from negotiation intelligence accumulated over years of services work - the kind of proprietary data that differentiates AI procurement tools, but one must have procurement experience and access to such data. Still, the pattern is worth watching across enterprise software categories.  
Campbell's move to chairman keeps one founder involved in corporate and commercial strategy while transferring day-to-day leadership to the executive who built its product and intelligence platform. The succession comes as Tropic seeks to turn its growing repository of procurement data into a larger role in how enterprises buy and manage software and AI.
### Why this matters for executives and strategy  
The Tropic leadership change shows how AI procurement tools are moving from experimental features to core infrastructure. With more than 100,000 negotiations feeding its benchmarks, Tropic is competing on data scale rather than product novelty. That means enterprise buyers should evaluate AI procurement tools on the quality and breadth of their underlying data, not just the interface features.  
It also means procurement teams with accumulated spend data have options: build AI tools internally, buy platforms like Tropic, or partner with providers. The strategic question for finance and procurement leadership is whether proprietary bidding history becomes a competitive asset - much like Tropic's own services business became the data source for its software platform.

results.name: Tropic Cinema Begins New Chapter Under PACKW | How the Community Can Help
results.content:
# A New Chapter for Tropic Cinema: Community Support Will Help Shape Its Future  
August 05, 2026 • Key West Tourist  
Key West has long been a place where creativity thrives. From the literary legacy of Tennessee Williams and Ernest Hemingway to generations of musicians, actors, filmmakers, painters, and storytellers, the island has earned a reputation as one of America's most vibrant arts communities.  
That creative tradition is entering an important new chapter.  
On August 4, 2026, Performing Arts Centers of Key West (PACKW) officially assumed responsibility for operating Tropic Cinema. The organization, which already manages the historic Tennessee Williams Theatre and the KeysTix ticketing platform, announced that it will oversee the cinema's daily operations while preserving its mission of bringing independent, documentary, foreign, and thought-provoking films to Key West audiences.  
For nearly three decades, the Key West Film Society built Tropic Cinema into far more than a movie theater. It became a gathering place where residents and visitors could experience independent cinema, filmmaker discussions, educational programs, cultural events, and films that often never reach traditional commercial theaters. Its impact extends well beyond entertainment, helping strengthen Key West's identity as a community that values creativity, education, and artistic expression.
According to PACKW Executive Director Matthew Rawls, the goal is not to change what makes Tropic Cinema special but to provide the operational support needed to secure its future. The organization plans to preserve the theater's programming, membership, and community character while creating a sustainable path forward.  
However, the success of that effort depends on the community.  
PACKW has made it clear that reopening the theater—currently targeted for October 1—is directly tied to the level of public support received in the coming weeks. Ticket sales, memberships, donations, sponsorships, and volunteers will all play an important role in helping reopen the doors and keep them open for years to come.  
This moment extends beyond one building in Key West. Across the country, independent theaters, performing arts centers, historic cinemas, and nonprofit cultural organizations continue to face financial pressures. Every successful preservation effort demonstrates what is possible when communities recognize the long-term value of investing in the arts.  
The Tennessee Williams Theatre, itself named for one of America's most celebrated playwrights who called Key West home for decades, has long served as an anchor for performing arts in the Florida Keys. Together with Tropic Cinema, these institutions represent a living connection between Key West's remarkable artistic past and its creative future.
Artists, playwrights, actors, filmmakers, musicians, writers, educators, and arts supporters understand that cultural institutions do far more than host performances or screen films. They inspire young artists, foster meaningful conversations, preserve local history, strengthen tourism, and create spaces where diverse voices can be heard.  
For anyone who has ever been inspired by an independent film, attended a community performance, discovered a new playwright, or simply believes that the arts enrich our lives, this is an opportunity to help preserve an important piece of Key West's cultural landscape.  
Whether through purchasing tickets, renewing memberships, volunteering time, making donations, or simply sharing the story, every contribution helps strengthen the future of one of the Florida Keys' most cherished cultural institutions.  
Communities that invest in the arts invest in themselves. With the continued support of Key West residents and arts enthusiasts everywhere, Tropic Cinema has the opportunity to begin an exciting new chapter while continuing the mission that has made it such an important part of island life for nearly 30 years.
